tactics.name: Anchoring
tactics.description: Setting the initial reference point in a negotiation to influence all subsequent offers
tactics.example: Starting with 'The market rate is typically 100K' before revealing your 80K offer
tactics.counter: Ignore the anchor and reframe with your own data: 'Based on our analysis, the value is...'

tactics.name: Mirroring
tactics.description: Repeating the last few words of what someone said to encourage them to elaborate
tactics.counter: Be aware you're being prompted to reveal more, stay concise

tactics.name: False Urgency
tactics.description: Creating artificial time pressure to force quick decisions
tactics.example: 'This offer expires tonight' or 'We have other interested buyers'
tactics.counter: Call the bluff: 'If this is the right deal, it will be right next week too'

tactics.name: Good Cop Bad Cop
tactics.description: Two negotiators playing opposing roles to manipulate emotions
tactics.example: One person is harsh, another is friendly and offers a 'compromise'
tactics.counter: Recognize the pattern and address both as a single position

tactics.name: Calibrated Questions
tactics.description: Open-ended questions starting with 'How' or 'What' that give control
tactics.example: 'How am I supposed to do that?' instead of 'I can't do that'
tactics.counter: Prepare for 'How' questions, they're harder to refuse than direct nos

tactics.name: Labeling
tactics.example: 'It seems like you're frustrated with this timeline'
tactics.counter: Confirms feeling without committing to change

tactics.name: Accusation Audit
tactics.description: Preemptively listing all negative things they might think about you
tactics.example: 'You probably think we're being unreasonable and asking for too much'
tactics.counter: Disarms negative perceptions before they solidify

tactics.name: BATNA Reveal
tactics.description: Showing you have a strong alternative to create pressure
tactics.example: 'We have another vendor offering similar terms'
tactics.counter: Show your BATNA is stronger: 'We're talking to 3 other clients'

tactics.name: Nibbling
tactics.description: Asking for small extras after the main deal is agreed
tactics.example: After agreeing to price: 'Can you also include free shipping?'
tactics.counter: Set clear boundaries: 'The package we agreed includes X, Y, Z only'

tactics.name: Flinching
tactics.description: Showing strong negative reaction to an offer to make them reconsider
tactics.example: Physical or verbal shock: 'Wow, that's way higher than expected'
tactics.counter: Acknowledge but hold firm: 'I understand it's high, here's why...'

tactics.name: Silence
tactics.description: Strategic pause after a statement to create discomfort and encourage concessions
tactics.example: After stating your price, say nothing and wait
tactics.counter: Be comfortable with silence, don't fill it with concessions

tactics.name: Trade-off
tactics.description: Never give without getting something in return
tactics.example: 'If we agree to your timeline, can you increase the budget by 10%?'
tactics.counter: Always tie concessions to reciprocal benefits

tactics.name: Decoy Effect
tactics.description: Presenting three options where middle option looks best by comparison
tactics.counter: Evaluate each option independently against your needs

tactics.name: Bogey
tactics.description: Pretending something is very important to you when it's not, to trade it later
tactics.example: Making a big deal about delivery date, then 'giving it up' for price concession
tactics.counter: Test if issues are real: 'If we solve X, are we good to close?'

tactics.name: Split the Difference
tactics.description: Suggesting to meet in the middle (often after anchoring high)
tactics.counter: Counter with: 'Let's look at the value drivers instead of splitting'
